SEARCH

All Classes and Interfaces

Class
Description
Achievement
Feats the player can accomplish.
AchievementTracker
Notices achievements earned during one run.
Actor
Anything that takes turns: the player, monsters, and timed effects.
Armor
Body armor.
Armor.Kind
Armor kinds.
AsciiRenderer
Renders a floor as text.
AttackProfile
Everything about one attack that the attacker contributes: how accurate it is, how hard it hits, and what it may inflict.
AttackResult
What happened in one attack.
AudioPlayer
Plays the game's music and sound effects.
BossAi
Phase changes for bosses.
CloseDoorCommand
Closes an adjacent open door.
Combat
Carries out attacks during play: resolves them with CombatResolver using the session's combat random stream, reports what happened in the message log, wakes the victim, and handles deaths.
CombatResolver
The combat formulas.
Command
A single player action.
CommandCodec
Converts recorded tokens back into actions.
CommandResult
The outcome of executing a Command.
Companion
Doc, a black-and-gold tiger cub who joins the player after they rub the Atrium's tiger statue.
CompanionAi
Doc's decisions, in priority order: attack an adjacent monster; if healthy, chase the nearest monster the player can see within CompanionAi.HUNT_RANGE; otherwise stay within CompanionAi.FOLLOW_DISTANCE tiles of the player. Doc ignores sleeping monsters unless they are adjacent, so Doc will not wake a whole room.
Conversations
What happens when the player talks to each NPC: dialogue, starting and finishing quests, rewards, and services.
CorridorCarver
Second generation step: connects rooms with L-shaped corridors and then turns suitable wall openings into doors.
Creature
A living thing that occupies a tile on a floor: the player, monsters and NPCs.
DamageType
Kinds of damage.
Difficulty
How hard a run is.
Direction
The eight compass directions a creature can step on the dungeon grid.
DropCommand
Drops a whole stack from the pack onto the floor.
DungeonGenerator
Builds a random floor for a depth from a seed.
EffectManager
The set of status effects currently on one creature.
EffectManager.Outcome
What happened when an effect was applied.
EffectType
The status effects a creature can be under, with how repeated applications combine.
EffectType.Stacking
How a new application combines with an existing effect of the same type.
EquippableItem
A weapon or armor.
EventBus
A minimal synchronous publish/subscribe hub for GameEvents.
Examiner
Describes what the player knows about a tile, for the examine (look) mode.
Experience
The experience curve and level-up rewards.
FieldOfView
Computes which tiles are visible from a point using recursive shadowcasting.
FixedFloorSource
A FloorSource that serves a fixed list of hand-drawn layouts, one per depth starting at depth 0.
FixedLayouts
Hand-drawn floor layouts.
Floor
A single dungeon floor: a rectangular grid of Terrain plus what the player has seen.
FloorContents
Everything on one floor besides its terrain: monsters, friendly NPCs, traps and piles of items.
FloorParser
Builds a Floor from a hand-written text layout, one string per row.
FloorSource
Supplies floors to the game session the first time the player reaches each depth.
FloorValidator
Checks that a generated floor is playable.
FloorView
Read-only view of a dungeon floor.
Food
Something to eat, which staves off hunger.
Food.Kind
Food kinds.
GameEvent
Something noteworthy that happened during a turn.
GameEvent.Type
Kinds of game events.
GameEventListener
Receives GameEvents published by a GameSession.
GameFactory
Creates fully configured game sessions.
GamePhase
The overall state of a run.
GameRules
Global game constants: timing, visibility and dungeon size.
GameSession
The central object of a run: owns the floors, the player, the turn scheduler and the message log, and is the only entry point for player actions.
GameView
The main game screen: the map in the center, a status panel on the right and the message log at the bottom.
GameView.Listener
Receives the player's requests to leave the game screen.
Gold
A pile of gold coins.
HallsApp
The JavaFX application: moves between the title screen and the game, and handles saving, loading and high scores.
Hazards
Spreading fire.
HighScoreTable
The best HighScoreTable.CAPACITY runs, highest score first.
HighScoreTable.Entry
One finished run.
Identification
What the player knows about item kinds in this run.
Inventory
The player's pack: an ordered list of item stacks with a fixed number of slots.
Item
Something that can lie on the floor and be carried.
ItemCategory
Broad groups of items, each with the symbol used to draw it on the floor.
ItemGenerator
Creates random items.
KeyItem
A key that opens the locked vault on one particular floor, or (a master key) on any floor.
Launcher
Program entry point.
LifetimeStats
Totals across every finished run (tutorials excluded), kept in a simple key=value text file by SaveStore.
LineOfSight
Straight-line tracing between two grid positions, used for thrown items, ranged attacks and targeting.
LootPlacer
Scatters items and gold across a generated floor.
MessageLog
A bounded history of messages shown to the player.
MessageLog.Entry
One line of the log.
Monster
A hostile creature.
Monster.State
What the monster is currently doing.
MonsterAbilities
Special reactions some monsters have during combat.
MonsterAi
Monster decision making: a small state machine per monster.
MonsterPopulator
Places the starting monsters on a generated floor.
MonsterTrait
Special behaviors a monster type can have.
MonsterType
The monster roster.
MoveCommand
Moves the player one tile.
Npc
A friendly character or fixture the player can talk to by walking into it.
Npc.Role
Who (or what) the NPC is.
Pathfinder
Grid path planning over a floor's terrain using 8-way movement.
Perk
Permanent bonuses the player chooses at certain levels.
PickUpCommand
Picks up the top item of the pile under the player (the most recently dropped).
Player
The adventurer controlled by the user.
Player.Hunger
How well fed the player is.
Position
An immutable (column, row) coordinate on a dungeon floor grid.
Potion
A drinkable potion.
Potion.Kind
Potion kinds.
ProceduralFloorSource
The standard dungeon: the hand-drawn Atrium at depth 0, generated floors from depth 1 to 9, and the hand-drawn Sanctum at depth 10.
Quest
One quest and its progress.
Quest.Id
The quests in the game.
Quest.State
Lifecycle of a quest.
QuestItem
Items that matter to quests rather than to combat.
QuestItem.Kind
Kinds of quest item.
QuestLog
All quests in a run, plus the small amount of extra state they need.
RandomStream
Independent purposes for randomness.
ReplayRunner
Rebuilds a session from a RunRecord by starting a new run with the same seed, difficulty and name, and re-applying every recorded action.
ReplayTool
Replays a recorded run without opening a window and prints what happened.
ResidentPlacer
Places the hand-picked characters of the Halls: the Atrium's residents, Warden Deng, the three zone bosses, and the Hollow Registrar.
Rng
Source of randomness for all game rules.
Room
A rectangular room on a generated floor.
Room.Role
The part a room plays in the floor's layout.
RoomDecorator
Third generation step: decides what each room is for, decorates interiors, and places the staircases.
RoomPlacer
First generation step: scatters non-overlapping rectangular rooms across an empty floor and carves out their interiors.
RoomType
How a room's interior is decorated during generation.
RunRecord
Everything needed to recreate a run: the seed, difficulty, player name, and every action taken.
RunStats
Statistics collected over a run, used for the end-of-run summary and the score.
SaveStore
Reads and writes the game's files in one directory (by default ~/.halls7800): "current-run.txt" — the saved, unfinished run "last-run.txt" — the record of the most recently finished run, kept for bug reports "scores.txt" — the high-score table "achievements.txt" — achievements earned in any run "lifetime-stats.txt" — totals across all finished runs
ScoreCalculator
Computes a run's score.
Screen
One full-window screen of the application (title screen or game).
Scroll
A single-use magic scroll.
Scroll.Kind
Scroll kinds.
SearchCommand
Spends a turn carefully searching the surrounding tiles for secret doors and hidden traps.
SeedDeriver
Derives independent seeds from a single run seed.
Shop
Conover's Curio & Circuit, the Atrium shop.
Sound
The game's sound effects.
SplitMixRng
Deterministic random number generator based on the SplitMix64 algorithm.
StairsCommand
Takes the staircase the player is standing on, either down or up.
StatusEffect
One active status effect on a creature: its type, turns remaining, and strength.
Terrain
The kinds of ground a floor tile can have, and the movement/visibility rules each one implies.
ThrowCommand
Throws one missile from a pack slot at the nearest visible monster within range.
ThrownWeapon
Stackable missiles thrown at a distant target.
ThrownWeapon.Kind
Missile kinds.
TitleScreen
The opening screen: the story of the Halls, the adventurer's name, difficulty, and the main menu (new game, Orientation tutorial, continue, high scores, quit).
TitleScreen.Actions
What the player chose on the title screen.
Trap
A trap hidden in the floor.
Trap.Type
Kinds of trap.
TrapPlacer
Hides traps on a generated floor: on plain floor tiles in corridors and ordinary rooms, never in the entrance room or within TrapPlacer.SAFE_RADIUS tiles of the arrival point, and never on stairs.
Traps
Trap effects and searching for hidden things.
Tune
Original chiptune music.
TurnScheduler
Orders the actions of all actors on the current floor by game time.
TutorialFloorSource
The Orientation tutorial ("level 0"): a single hand-drawn floor of five rooms, each with signs that explain one part of the game.
UseItemCommand
Uses the item in a pack slot in the natural way: wield or remove a weapon, put on or take off armor, drink a potion, read a scroll, eat food, or zap a wand at the nearest monster.
WaitCommand
Lets one normal action's worth of time pass without doing anything.
Wand
A magic wand with a limited number of charges.
Wand.Kind
Wand kinds.
WandZapper
Fires wand bolts.
Weapon
A melee weapon.
Weapon.Kind
Weapon kinds.
WeightedTable<T>
A list of choices with relative weights, for picking room types, monsters, loot, and so on.
Zone
The themed regions of the dungeon and the generation parameters for each.
